node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Picture graph key interpretation
node.description: Use the key in a picture graph to determine how many data values each symbol or part-symbol represents.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Partial symbol interpretation
node.description: Interpret half symbols or other partial symbols in picture graphs using the graph key.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bar height as frequency
node.description: Interpret the height or length of a bar as the frequency for its category.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bar spacing for categories
node.description: Use gaps between bars to show that a bar graph represents separate categories rather than continuous intervals.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Vertical axis scale reading
node.description: Read values between marked scale labels on a graph axis using equal intervals.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Truncated axis detection
node.description: Identify when a graph axis does not start at zero or uses a restricted range that may exaggerate differences.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dot stack frequency
node.description: Interpret stacked dots above the same value as repeated observations with that value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dot plot value axis
node.description: Read the value represented by each dot using the number-line axis of a dot plot.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Line plot fraction measurements
node.description: Represent measurement data such as halves, quarters or eighths on a line plot with a fractional scale.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Display centre spread and shape language
node.description: Describe a distribution from a visual display using centre, spread, shape, clusters, gaps and outliers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Stem-and-leaf key interpretation
node.description: Use the key of a stem-and-leaf plot to determine the place value represented by stems and leaves.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Ordered leaves
node.description: Order leaves within each stem so a stem-and-leaf plot preserves the ordered data values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Split stems
node.description: Use split stems to spread crowded stem-and-leaf plots while preserving the data values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Interval width choice
node.description: Choose a sensible interval width for grouped numerical data so the display shows useful structure without excessive detail or overgrouping.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Interval boundary inclusion
node.description: Decide which interval contains a boundary value using non-overlapping interval rules.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Histogram bin height as frequency
node.description: Interpret the height of a histogram bar as the frequency or relative frequency for a numerical interval.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Adjacent bars in histograms
node.description: Recognise that histogram bars touch because adjacent intervals represent a continuous numerical scale.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Relative frequency histogram introduction
node.description: Interpret a histogram where bar heights show proportions or percentages rather than raw frequencies.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box plot five-number summary
node.description: Connect the minimum, lower quartile, median, upper quartile and maximum to the features of a box plot.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box plot median and quartiles
node.description: Read the median and quartiles from a box plot and connect them to the ordered data set.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box plot whiskers and range
node.description: Interpret whiskers as showing the lower and upper spread of data beyond the box, usually to minimum and maximum values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Compare box plots by centre and spread
node.description: Compare two or more box plots using medians, interquartile ranges, ranges and possible outliers.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Choose display for data type
node.description: Choose a suitable display by considering whether the data are categorical, numerical, grouped, paired or comparative.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Misleading display detection
node.description: Identify misleading design choices in data displays, including distorted scales, missing labels, selective ranges and inappropriate graph types.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Context caption for data display
node.description: Write a short caption that states what the display shows, including context, variable, group and units where relevant.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bar height encodes frequency
node.description: In a bar graph, the bar height or length represents the frequency for the category, read using the graph scale.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dot stack shows repeated values
node.description: Multiple dots above the same value show multiple observations with that value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Stem-and-leaf key sets place value
node.description: The key in a stem-and-leaf plot explains how stems and leaves combine to make actual data values.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Histogram bars touch for intervals
node.description: Histogram bars touch because they represent adjacent intervals on a numerical scale rather than separate categories.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box plots compare median IQR and range
node.description: Box plots support comparison of distributions using median, interquartile range and overall range rather than every individual value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Bar height read without scale
node.description: Learner reads bar heights by visual size alone instead of using the axis scale.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Dot plot dots are categories
node.description: Learner treats each dot as a separate category rather than one observation at a numerical value.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Stem-and-leaf leaf is decimal
node.description: Learner reads a stem-and-leaf value as a decimal or separate number rather than using the key to combine stem and leaf.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Histogram needs gaps between bars
node.description: Learner draws gaps between histogram bars because they confuse histograms with category bar graphs.

node.subject: Mathematics
node.label: Box contains all data
node.description: Learner thinks the box in a box plot contains all data values rather than the middle half of the data.

edge.rationale: Interpreting a key is central to many-to-one symbol picture graphs.
Reading bar height is central to reading a bar graph.
Reading stacked dots is central to interpreting dot plots.
The key is essential to interpreting stem-and-leaf plots.
Histogram interpretation includes connecting interval bars to frequencies.
Five-number summary features are central to box plot interpretation.
Choosing a display is part of comparing the usefulness of data displays.
Interpreting a picture graph key builds on the idea that one symbol may stand for multiple data values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts each symbol as one even when the key says otherwise.

edge.rationale: Partial symbols can be interpreted only after using the graph key.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats a half symbol as one full symbol or ignores it.

edge.rationale: Bar-height interpretation is a focused part of reading bar graphs.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares bars visually without reading the scale.

edge.rationale: Understanding bar spacing depends on recognising categorical data as separate groups.
edge.failure_signal: Learner treats category bars as continuous intervals.

edge.rationale: Reading between tick marks depends on understanding equal graph scales.
edge.failure_signal: Learner misreads values between labelled axis intervals.

edge.rationale: Detecting truncated axes requires reading the scale and starting value of the axis.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts exaggerated differences caused by a shortened axis.

edge.rationale: Stacked-dot interpretation is a focused part of reading dot plots.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts only distinct x-values and misses repeated data values.

edge.rationale: After understanding dot frequency, learners must map each stack to its value on the axis.
edge.failure_signal: Learner counts dots but cannot identify their numerical values.

edge.rationale: Fractional line plots extend line plots for measurement data to fractional scales.
edge.failure_signal: Learner places fractional measurements unevenly or at whole-number positions only.

edge.rationale: Centre-spread-shape descriptions build on identifying clusters, gaps and outliers.
edge.failure_signal: Learner describes only individual values rather than overall distribution features.

edge.rationale: Stem-and-leaf plots display numerical data, so learners must first distinguish numerical from categorical data.
edge.failure_signal: Learner applies stem-and-leaf structure to category labels or misreads numerical values.

edge.rationale: Ordering leaves requires knowing how leaves combine with stems to make data values.
edge.failure_signal: Learner writes leaves in collection order and loses the ordered-data feature of the display.

edge.rationale: Split stems are an extension of ordered stem-and-leaf construction when stems are crowded.
edge.failure_signal: Learner splits stems without preserving the correct value ranges.

edge.rationale: Choosing interval width builds on grouping numerical data into intervals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses intervals that are too narrow, too broad or uneven without purpose.

edge.rationale: Boundary rules are needed after intervals have been defined.
edge.failure_signal: Learner double-counts or omits values that fall on interval boundaries.

edge.rationale: Reading bin height is a focused part of histogram interpretation.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads a histogram bar as an individual data value instead of an interval frequency.

edge.rationale: Adjacent bars follow from using contiguous non-overlapping intervals.
edge.failure_signal: Learner inserts category-style gaps between histogram bars.

edge.rationale: Relative-frequency histograms use the same interval structure but scale heights as proportions or percentages.
edge.failure_signal: Learner confuses relative frequency with raw count frequency.

edge.rationale: Box plots display the five-number summary, so learners need the summary values first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner cannot connect minimum, quartiles and maximum to box plot features.

edge.rationale: Median and quartile reading is part of interpreting the five-number summary in a box plot.
edge.failure_signal: Learner reads the edge of the box as the mean or as all data values.

edge.rationale: Whisker interpretation depends on understanding the minimum and maximum positions in the five-number summary.
edge.failure_signal: Learner thinks whisker length shows number of data values rather than spread.

edge.rationale: Comparing box plots requires reading median and quartile features first.
edge.failure_signal: Learner compares only box widths or total graph size without referencing centre and spread.

edge.rationale: Display choice depends on whether the data are categorical or numerical and whether they are grouped or comparative.
edge.failure_signal: Learner chooses a histogram for nominal categories or a bar graph for continuous intervals without justification.

edge.rationale: Evaluating misleading displays requires knowing what display and scale choices are appropriate.
edge.failure_signal: Learner accepts a visually persuasive display despite distorted scale or inappropriate type.

edge.rationale: Writing a useful caption depends on understanding labels, titles, units and context.
edge.failure_signal: Learner presents a graph without saying what data, group or unit it represents.
